newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse down, off earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse down, off earlier lows.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade lower on Monday amid evidence of profit-taking after last week's highs, but off earlier lows and keeping an eye out for U.S. data due in the afternoon.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended down 7.19 points, or 0.27 percent, at 2,651.85 points while the December DAX futures contract was down 12 points at 2,665.

Dealers blamed the fall-off to a mild bout of profit-taking after the DAX surged to record highs last week but said many investors steered clear of the market in the absence of any meaningful corporate news.
Support came from the dollar, which was steady at a strong 1.5274 against the mark.
U.S. data due this afternoon, including new home sales and the Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index, could help to inject some life into the market, dealers said.

Profit-taking hit the chemical sector particularly hard. BASF AG extended its losses from Friday, when it fell on news that a U.S. advisory committee had recommending withholding approval for a new BASF drug, Meridia.
BASF recovered somewhat over the session to end bourse down 10 pfennigs at 48 marks.
Meanwhile Degussa Ag ended bourse trade down 2.50 marks at 552.50 marks, again hit by profit-taking having earlier risen on news it planned to up its stake in Muro Pharmaceuticals in the U.S.
